html:
The Shining Path was a Maoist guerrilla movement in Peru, founded by the philosophy professor Abimael Guzmán, that began an armed war on 17 May 1980 by burning ballot boxes. The war killed about 70,000 people.

It grew in the poor highland region of Ayacucho, where Guzmán taught. It aimed to destroy the state and surround the cities from the countryside. It killed village leaders, aid workers and whole communities that resisted, and bombed Lima. The army and police, in turn, massacred peasants. Most of the dead were Quechua-speaking villagers.

Police captured Guzmán in a Lima house in September 1992, without a shot, and the movement fell apart. A truth commission found in 2003 that the Shining Path was responsible for about half of the deaths. The war shaped the rule of Fujimori and left deep scars in Peru, in the same region as the Battle of Ayacucho.
sum: The Shining Path was a Maoist guerrilla movement in Peru, founded by the philosophy professor Abimael Guzmán, that began an armed war on 17 May 1980 by burning ballot boxes. The war killed about 70,000 people.
